tool_analysis:
Step Analysis: The recorded session logs into Magento admin, navigates to the Sales > Orders grid, explores and interacts with all relevant filters (order #, date range, store view, status, base and purchased grand totals, billing/shipping names), uses Search and Reset Filter, changes per-page size, uses pagination, and clicks View links. Previous failures were due to waiting for a fragile autogenerated element ID. This attempt relied instead on semantic selectors and demonstrated that controls are stable.

Task Definition: Build a reusable tool that, given various optional filter parameters and simple pagination flags, opens the Magento admin Sales Orders grid, optionally resets filters, applies provided criteria, optionally paginates, clicks an appropriate 'View' link, and finally returns structured information about the current grid rows and their View URLs. The tool must avoid brittle selectors like #id_df0dc655a6c37ba9fce5d13194ce7e86 and instead use robust, semantic selectors.

Action Plan:
1) Navigate directly to the Sales Orders grid URL.
2) Close the notification popup if present so filters are accessible.
3) Optionally reset existing filters (if requested) via the 'Reset Filter' button.
4) Fill in any provided filter fields in the filter row: Any/Yes/No virtual selector, Order #, Purchased From (Store) dropdown, Purchased On date range, Bill to Name, Ship to Name, G.T. (Base) and G.T. (Purchased) numeric ranges, Status dropdown.
5) Optionally adjust the per-page selector (View X per page).
6) Click the Search button to apply filters and wait for the grid to reload.
7) Optionally click the Next page pagination control once and wait for reload.
8) Click an appropriate View link: either the one whose Order # matches a provided target increment ID or the first data row if not specified. Use an agentic step because row positions and order IDs vary.
9) Extract structured data from the grid (or from the order detail view if navigated) including order-level columns and View URLs, returning it as the tool output.

Variable Identification: Inputs are all the actual filter fields and behavioural flags seen on the grid:
- order_increment_id: text in 'Order #' filter.
- purchased_from_store: visible option text in the store view dropdown.
- purchased_on_from / purchased_on_to: date range values in MM/DD/YYYY.
- billing_name: Bill to Name filter text.
- shipping_name: Ship to Name filter text.
- base_grand_total_from / base_grand_total_to: numeric range for G.T. (Base).
- purchased_grand_total_from / purchased_grand_total_to: numeric range for G.T. (Purchased).
- status: visible text of Status dropdown options (Complete, Pending, etc.).
- is_virtual: Any/Yes/No selector in first filter column.
- per_page: View X per page selector (20/30/50/100/200).
- go_to_next_page: flag indicating whether to paginate once forwards.
- reset_filters_first: flag to clear filters before applying new criteria.
- target_order_increment_id_for_view: which order's View link to click.
- login_required: mostly informational; session is assumed authenticated but retained as an optional behavior flag.

Step Optimization: 
- Navigation is a single deterministic step to the known sales_order URL; no need to go through menu clicks.
- Instead of waiting for any particular dynamic element ID, the tool uses CSS selectors rooted in known IDs and names used by Magento grids (e.g., #sales_order_grid_filter_real_order_id, input[name*='increment_id'], select[name*='store_id']). These selectors are stable and should match exactly one element on the Sales Orders grid because Magento uses unique filter field IDs per column.
- The notification popup close is implemented as a click on its close anchor with a generic but tight selector (a.notice-close or onclick containing 'closeMessage'), and any failure to find it is harmless.
- For filter inputs and dropdowns, each step uses attribute-based selectors that resolve to a single element within the grid filter row. These are deterministic interactions; no elementHash-based selectors are required and we avoid the previously failing #id_df0dc655a6c37ba9fce5d13194ce7e86.
- The per-page selector and pagination controls are targeted by their pager context and attributes like title='Next page' or onchange*='setPageLimit', which are stable across reloads.
- Because the specific row containing a given order increment ID can vary with filters and sorting, an agentic step is used to locate and click the appropriate 'View' link; this avoids brittle assumptions about row indices.
- Finally, a single extract_page_content step returns the relevant order data instead of multiple low-level cell extractions. The tool is strictly focused on order search and retrieval; mass actions, exports, RSS, and other unrelated controls are intentionally omitted.

This design directly addresses the previous failure by eliminating dependence on dynamic autogenerated element IDs and by adding modest waits around grid reloads. It also parameterizes all relevant filter fields while keeping every step essential to searching and viewing orders.
name: tool_search_orders_v3
description: Search Magento admin sales orders using flexible filters (order number, date range, store, billing/shipping name, grand total ranges, status) plus pagination and per-page size; returns grid rows and View links.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento admin Sales Orders grid URL.
Close the notification popup if present by clicking its 'close' link; selector targets the notice close anchor.
Wait briefly to ensure the orders grid and filters are fully loaded.
If reset_filters_first is true, click the 'Reset Filter' button to clear existing filters.
Type the order increment ID into the 'Order #' filter input if order_increment_id is provided.
Choose store view in 'Purchased From (Store)' filter dropdown if purchased_from_store is provided.
Fill 'Purchased On' From date input if purchased_on_from is provided (MM/DD/YYYY).
Fill 'Purchased On' To date input if purchased_on_to is provided (MM/DD/YYYY).
Enter text into 'Bill to Name' filter if billing_name is provided.
Enter text into 'Ship to Name' filter if shipping_name is provided.
Fill 'G.T. (Base)' From amount if base_grand_total_from is provided.
Fill 'G.T. (Base)' To amount if base_grand_total_to is provided.
Fill 'G.T. (Purchased)' From amount if purchased_grand_total_from is provided.
Fill 'G.T. (Purchased)' To amount if purchased_grand_total_to is provided.
Select order status in 'Status' filter dropdown if status is provided.
Set first-column Any/Yes/No filter for virtual orders if is_virtual is provided.
Change 'View X per page' selector to requested page size if per_page is provided.
Click the 'Search' button to apply all configured filters.
Wait for the orders grid to reload after applying filters.
If go_to_next_page is true, click the 'Next page' pagination control once.
Wait for the grid to load the next page if pagination was triggered.
Use reasoning to reliably locate and click the correct 'View' link because row positions and order numbers vary dynamically.
steps.task: On the current Sales Orders grid, find the row whose 'Order #' cell matches {target_order_increment_id_for_view} (or the first data row if no ID is provided) and click its 'View' link in the 'Action' column.

steps.description: Return structured order data and View URLs for the caller to consume.
steps.goal: From the current page (orders grid or specific order view), extract a structured list of orders currently visible with their Order #, Purchased From (Store), Purchased On, Bill to Name, Ship to Name, G.T. (Base), G.T. (Purchased), Status, and the absolute URL of their 'View' link. If on an order detail page, also provide the main order info header and order number.

steps.description: Final short wait to ensure all async content is stable for extraction.

input_schema.name: order_increment_id
input_schema.description: Filter for order number (Increment ID) shown in the 'Order #' column, e.g. 000000299

input_schema.name: purchased_from_store
input_schema.description: Visible text of the store view in the 'Purchased From (Store)' filter dropdown, e.g. 'English' or 'Main Website Store'

input_schema.name: purchased_on_from
input_schema.description: Lower bound of purchase date range (From) under 'Purchased On' column, format MM/DD/YYYY

input_schema.name: purchased_on_to
input_schema.description: Upper bound of purchase date range (To) under 'Purchased On' column, format MM/DD/YYYY

input_schema.name: billing_name
input_schema.description: Text to filter by 'Bill to Name' column

input_schema.name: shipping_name
input_schema.description: Text to filter by 'Ship to Name' column

input_schema.name: base_grand_total_from
input_schema.description: Lower bound of grand total range in base currency (From) under 'G.T. (Base)' column

input_schema.name: base_grand_total_to
input_schema.description: Upper bound of grand total range in base currency (To) under 'G.T. (Base)' column

input_schema.name: purchased_grand_total_from
input_schema.description: Lower bound of grand total range in purchased currency (From) under 'G.T. (Purchased)' column

input_schema.name: purchased_grand_total_to
input_schema.description: Upper bound of grand total range in purchased currency (To) under 'G.T. (Purchased)' column

input_schema.name: status
input_schema.description: Visible text of the order status in the 'Status' filter dropdown, e.g. 'Complete', 'Pending', 'Processing'

input_schema.name: is_virtual
input_schema.description: First-column selector in filter row for virtual orders; visible options Any/Yes/No

input_schema.name: per_page
input_schema.description: Number of results per page to select from the 'View X per page' control

input_schema.name: go_to_next_page
input_schema.description: If true, click the 'Next page' pagination control once after applying filters

input_schema.name: reset_filters_first
input_schema.description: If true, click 'Reset Filter' before applying any new filter values

input_schema.name: target_order_increment_id_for_view
input_schema.description: If provided, click the 'View' link in the row whose 'Order #' matches this increment ID; otherwise click the first 'View' link

input_schema.name: login_required
input_schema.description: If true, indicates that login may be needed (tool assumes session is already authenticated but can be used to skip login-related checks)
